mainTopic: רב נחמן's regret, שמואל's rule on forgiving a sold שטר חוב, and how and in what order debts are paid
overview: This amud opens at the end of a story. רב נחמן hinted that a daughter could forgive her late mother's sold כתובה, so the money would stay with her father and she would later inherit it. He then regretted acting like עורכי הדיינין, because an אדם חשוב must avoid even looking like he favors family. The גמרא returns to שמואל's rule behind the story: a seller of a שטר חוב, and even his heir, can still forgive the debt. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע shows the buyer how to protect himself, and אמימר rules that what the seller owes the buyer depends on דינא דגרמי. In a real case, רב אשי made the seller pay the note's full value. אמימר in the name of רב חמא then teaches that a בעל חוב is paid with money and a wife's כתובה with land, and that when there is only one field, the creditor gets it. רב פפא learns that forcing a debtor to sell his land was only a penalty for a cheat. Finally, רב כהנא asks what happens if a debtor refuses the מצוה of repaying. רב פפא answers with a ברייתא about forcing positive מצוות, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The daughter takes the hint and forgives the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The story ends with רב נחמן's hint: the daughter can forgive her mother's sold כתובה so it stays with her father, and she does it.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Isn't there someone to tell her) that she should go and forgive her mother's כתובה for her father, and then inherit it from him? She heard, went, and forgave it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing a story from the previous page. רב נחמן hinted out loud that the daughter could cancel the debt in her mother's sold כתובה, and she went and did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother sold her כתובה to buyers and then died, so her daughter inherited her rights. Under שמואל's rule, the daughter could forgive the father's debt, which wipes out what the buyers paid for. The money then stays with the father, and the daughter will inherit it from him.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract: a husband's written debt to his wife.
Forgive it: cancel a debt.
She will inherit it.

steps.confusionAlert: The daughter is not taking money from her father. She is canceling a debt her father owed, and the people who bought the כתובה are the ones who lose.

phrases.english: that she should go and forgive her mother's כתובה
phrases.notes: This line continues from the previous page, where רב נחמן said out loud, 'Isn't there anyone who will tell her...'

phrases.english: for her father, and she will inherit it from him?
She heard, went, and forgave it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רב נחמן's hint, the daughter forgave the כתובה debt so that the money would stay with her father.

steps.title: רב נחמן regrets acting like a lawyer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says he made himself like someone who coaches people on how to win their case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: We made ourselves like those who coach the litigants before judges.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן looks back and regrets his hint. He says he acted like a lawyer giving tactics instead of a neutral judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A judge is supposed to stay neutral and not give one side strategy. By hinting how the daughter could win, רב נחמן crossed that line, and he admits it.

keyTerms.meaning: People who coach litigants on how to argue before judges, like lawyers.
We made ourselves (into).

steps.whyThisMatters: רב נחמן uses the well-known warning against acting like עורכי הדיינין to judge his own act. Even a quiet hint meant to help a relative counts as coaching one side.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
We have made ourselves like advisors of judges.
phrases.notes: He means people who coach one side on how to win, like lawyers do.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב נַחְמָן: עָשִׂינוּ עַצְמֵינוּ כְּעוֹרְכֵי הַדַּיָּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן reacts to what happened in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving one side strategy is improper for a judge.

steps.title: Why did רב נחמן change his mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב נחמן held at first and what he held at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the start, what did he hold, and at the end, what did he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן first gave the hint and then regretted it. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If giving the hint was wrong, why did a great judge do it? And if it was right, why did he regret it? The גמרא wants the reasoning behind each of his two positions.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, at the start.
In the end.
What did he hold? What was his reasoning?

phrases.english: At the outset, what did he hold,
and in the end, what did he hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי סְבַר, וּלְבַסּוֹף מַאי סְבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind steps 1 and 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for רב נחמן's first position and the reason he changed it.

steps.title: Helping family versus the standard for an important person
steps.stepSummary: At first he relied on 'do not hide from your own flesh.' In the end he held that an important person is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the start he held: 'And do not hide yourself from your own flesh.' In the end he held: an important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both positions. First, רב נחמן felt obligated to help his relative. Later he decided that someone of his stature must avoid even the appearance of favoring family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that you should help your relatives, so giving advice seemed like a מצוה. But an אדם חשוב is held to a stricter standard, because people may think he bends judgment for family. So the same act that is fine for an ordinary person was wrong for him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not hide yourself from your own flesh': help your relatives.
An important or distinguished person.
Is different.

steps.whatToRemember: Helping family is a מצוה, but an אדם חשוב, especially a judge, must hold back to avoid looking biased.

phrases.english: At the outset he held:
"And from your own flesh do not hide yourself,"
and in the end he held: an important person is different.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First he followed the duty to help a relative. Later he held that an important person must avoid any look of favoritism.

steps.title: שמואל: a seller of a debt document can still forgive it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שמואל's rule: if you sell a שטר חוב and then forgive the debt, it is forgiven, and even an heir can forgive it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the matter itself. שמואל said: One who sells a promissory note to another and then forgives the debt, it is forgiven. And even an heir can forgive it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks directly at שמואל's rule, which is what made the daughter's move work. A seller of a debt document can still cancel the debt, and so can his heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower's obligation is really to the original lender. So even after the document is sold, the original lender can release the borrower. The heir stands in the lender's place, which is why the daughter could forgive her mother's כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': returning to a statement quoted earlier in order to discuss it.
A promissory note, a written record of a debt.
It is forgiven, the debt is canceled.
An heir.

steps.confusionAlert: Selling the שטר does not end the seller's power over the debt. The seller can still wipe it out, and the buyer loses.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Shmuel said:
One who sells a promissory note to another,
and then went back and forgave it, it is forgiven,
phrases.notes: He forgives the borrower, not the buyer, so the debt is gone and the buyer is left holding nothing.

phrases.english: and even an heir can forgive.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַמּוֹכֵר שְׁטַר חוֹב לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the rule of שמואל that the story relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller of a שטר חוב, or his heir, can still forgive the debt, and the forgiveness takes effect.

steps.title: How a smart buyer protects himself
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע advises the buyer to pay the borrower so he writes a new note in the buyer's own name.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: And if the buyer is smart, he jingles some coins for the borrower, and the borrower writes him a new document in the buyer's name.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the seller can cancel the debt, a buyer is at risk. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives a practical fix: pay the borrower to write a new note made out directly to the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the borrower owes the buyer directly in a new שטר, the original lender has nothing left to forgive. The small payment buys the buyer full security.

keyTerms.meaning: Smart, clever.
He jingles coins for him: pays him a little.
A document in his own name.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
And if he is smart,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the buyer of the document.

phrases.english: he jingles coins for him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the borrower. The buyer gives him some money.

phrases.english: and he writes him a document in his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וְאִי פִּקֵּחַ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives practical advice to get around the risk created by שמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer can protect himself by having the borrower write a new שטר in the buyer's name.

steps.title: What the seller owes the buyer: depends on דינא דגרמי
steps.stepSummary: אמימר: if one holds דינא דגרמי, the seller who forgave the debt pays the full value of the note; if not, only the value of the paper.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: One who rules by דינא דגרמי makes the seller pay the value of a good, valid document. One who does not rule by דינא דגרמי makes him pay only the value of the paper.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר deals with the buyer who lost out when the seller forgave the debt. How much he can collect from the seller depends on whether we hold someone liable for causing a loss indirectly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forgiving the debt did not touch the paper itself, but it made the document worthless, which counts as indirect damage. Under דינא דגרמי the seller pays the full amount the note was worth. Without it, he pays only for the plain paper.

keyTerms.meaning: The law holding a person liable for damage he causes indirectly.
He has him collect, makes him pay.
A good, valid document, worth its full face value.
Mere paper.

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: a seller can still forgive a sold debt. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: a smart buyer gets a new note in his own name. אמימר: what the seller owes the buyer depends on דינא דגרמי, either the full value or just the paper.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
One who rules according to the law of indirect damage
has him pay the value of a good document.
One who does not rule according to the law of indirect damage,
has him pay only the value of mere paper.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: מַאן דְּדָאֵין דִּינָא דִגְרָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what the buyer can recover after the seller forgives the debt under שמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under דינא דגרמי, the seller pays the note's full value. Without it, he pays only for the paper.

steps.title: A real case: רב אשי makes the seller pay the full value
steps.stepSummary: In a real case, רפרם pressured רב אשי to rule clearly, and רב אשי made the seller pay the full value of the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a real case. רפרם pressured רב אשי to give a clear ruling, and רב אשי made him pay as if he had damaged a valuable beam meant for sculptures. That means he paid the full value of the note.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows how the question of the forgiven שטר חוב was decided in practice. רב אשי made the seller pay the full amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said that whether the seller pays the full value depends on דינא דגרמי. Here a real ruling shows the full value was collected. That fits the view that holds דינא דגרמי, and so the abstract debate gets a practical outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: A real case or incident that came before a judge
He pressured him (pushed him to give a clear ruling)
He collected (had the money paid out)
A beam for sculptures. This is a picture for paying the full, high value.

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, the seller who sold a שטר חוב and then forgave the debt was made to pay its full value.

phrases.english: There was an incident
and Rafram pressured Rav Ashi,
and he collected in this case
like a beam for sculptures.
phrases.notes: Picture someone ruining a pricey beam meant for carving: he pays its full worth. Here that means the full value of the note.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא וְכַפְיֵיהּ רַפְרָם לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical ruling for אמימר's conditional statement about דינא דגרמי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, the full value of the note was collected from the seller who forgave the debt.

steps.title: Creditor gets money, wife gets land
steps.stepSummary: אמימר in the name of רב חמא: a man who owes both a כתובה and a regular debt pays the בעל חוב with money and the woman with land.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said in the name of רב חמא: Suppose a man owes his wife's כתובה and also owes a creditor, and he has both land and cash. We pay the creditor with cash and the woman with land. Each one is paid by the rule that fits that person.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It says how to pay two different kinds of debts when the man has both land and money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The creditor gave real money, so it is fair that he gets money back. The woman never handed over money. Her כתובה rests on the man's land, so she is paid with land.

keyTerms.meaning: The money a husband owes his wife under the marriage contract
A creditor, someone who lent money
We pay off, we settle the debt
Money, cash
Land

phrases.english: Ameimar said in the name of Rav Ḥama:
One who has upon himself
a wife's marriage contract and a creditor,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִית לֵיהּ אַרְעָא וְאִית לֵיהּ זוּזֵי —
phrases.english: and he has land and he has money —
the creditor, we pay him off with money,
the woman, we pay her off with land,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי כִּי דִינֵיהּ וְהַאי כִּי דִינֵיהּ.
phrases.english: this one according to his law, and that one according to her law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how different kinds of debts get paid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל חוב is paid with money; a כתובה is paid with land.

steps.title: Only one field: the creditor gets it
steps.stepSummary: If there is only one field and it covers only one debt, the בעל חוב gets it, because women want to marry even more than men do.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is only one field and it is enough for only one of them, we give it to the creditor and not to the woman. Why? A woman wants to get married even more than a man wants to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא's teaching continues with a harder case: there is only one field and two people want it. He gives it to the creditor and explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women do not marry for the sake of the כתובה, so favoring the creditor will not stop women from marrying. If creditors lost out, though, people would stop lending money. So the creditor comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: One
We give
What is the reason?

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the כתובה is less important. It only means that when there is not enough for both, the creditor is paid first, because women will marry anyway.
steps.whatToRemember: Normally: creditor gets money, wife gets land. If there is only one field, the creditor gets it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא אִיכָּא אֶלָּא חַד אַרְעָא
phrases.english: And if there is only one plot of land
and it is fit for only one —
phrases.notes: He means the field is only worth enough to pay one of the two debts.

phrases.english: we give it to the creditor,
we do not give it to the woman.
What is the reason?
More than a man wants to marry,
a woman wants to be married.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא אִיכָּא אֶלָּא חַד אַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב חמא's teaching with the case where the land is only enough for one person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With only one field, the creditor gets it, because favoring him will not discourage women from marrying.

steps.title: רב פפא asks if רבא said the debtor must sell the land himself
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks רב חמא whether he really quoted רבא as saying that a debtor who offers land must go sell it himself and pay cash.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רב חמא: Is it true that you say in the name of רבא this rule? A man owes money and has land. The creditor comes to collect, and the man says, 'Go take it from the land.' Do we tell the man, 'Go sell it yourself, and bring the money and give it to him'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא checks whether a report about רבא's ruling is accurate. He is setting up רב חמא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is related to step 9, where the creditor gets money. The question is whether the debtor must turn his land into cash for the creditor, or whether he can just hand over the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it certain/true? (used here as a question)
People are owed money by him; he owes money
Go sell

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרַב חָמָא:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rav Ḥama:
Is it true that you say in the name of Rava,
one who owes money,
and he has land,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא בַּעַל חוֹב וְקָא תָבַע מִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: and the creditor came and demands from him,
and he says to him: 'Go take from the land,'
we say to him: 'Go sell it yourself,'
'and bring the money and give it to him'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרַב חָמָא: וַדַּאי דְּאָמְרִיתוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that a creditor is paid with money by asking if the debtor must sell land to get cash.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב חמא really reported in the name of רבא that a debtor must sell his land himself and pay the creditor cash.

steps.title: רב חמא: No, I did not say that
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא answers that he did not say this in the name of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא answers רב פפא's question with one short word: No.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חמא denies that he quoted רבא this way. So the claim that a debtor must always sell his land and bring cash is not backed by רבא through רב חמא.

keyTerms.meaning: No

phrases.english: He said to him: No.
phrases.notes: רב חמא is saying he never quoted רבא this way.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חמא did not say in the name of רבא that the debtor must sell the land himself and pay cash.

steps.title: רב פפא asks for the real story
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks רב חמא what actually happened in the case that led people to quote רבא wrongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tell me the actual incident: how did it happen?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא just said he never quoted רבא's ruling as a general rule, so רב פפא asks what the real case was. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there was no general rule, there must have been a specific case that people misunderstood. רב פפא wants the facts so he can see why that ruling was given.

keyTerms.meaning: The incident itself, the actual story
How was it? What happened?

phrases.english: Tell me the incident itself,
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא speaking to רב חמא.

phrases.english: how did it happen?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא לִי גּוּפָא דְעוֹבָדָא הֵיכִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רב חמא's denial by asking for the real background case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual facts of the case that caused the ruling to be credited to רבא.

steps.title: The debtor was a cheat, so he was treated harshly
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא explains that the debtor falsely claimed his money belonged to a גוי, so בית דין forced him to sell his land and pay cash.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The man pretended his money belonged to a gentile. He acted improperly, so they acted improperly with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא tells the story: the debtor hid his cash by saying it belonged to a גוי. Because he cheated, בית דין made him sell his land and pay money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a debtor may pay with land. Here the ruling was an exception, a penalty for a dishonest debtor, and not a general rule. That is why it was wrong to quote it as רבא's general הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Hanging his money on a gentile, claiming his money belongs to a non-Jew
Improperly, not the normal fair way
Therefore

steps.whatToRemember: Forcing a debtor to sell his land and pay cash was a penalty for a cheating debtor, not the normal rule.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תּוֹלֶה מְעוֹתָיו בְּגוֹי הֲוָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: He was one who hung his money on a gentile,
phrases.notes: He had cash but claimed it belonged to a גוי, so the lender couldn't collect it.

phrases.english: he acted improperly,
therefore they acted improperly with him.
phrases.notes: "They" means בית דין, who made him sell his land and pay cash.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תּוֹלֶה מְעוֹתָיו בְּגוֹי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's request for the facts of the case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The debtor was dishonest, hiding his money under a גוי's name, so בית דין penalized him by forcing a sale.

steps.title: What if the debtor refuses the מצוה of repaying?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks רב פפא: if paying back a loan is a מצוה, what happens if the debtor says he does not want to do the מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to רב פפא: According to you, who say that paying a creditor is a מצוה, if the debtor says, "I don't want to do a מצוה," what happens?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא tests רב פפא's view that paying a debt is a מצוה. He asks what happens if the debtor simply refuses to do the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If repaying is only a מצוה and not a direct money obligation, it might seem the debtor could just choose not to do it. רב כהנא wants to know how בית דין could force him to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Paying back a creditor
A commandment, a religious duty
According to you, by your view
It does not suit me, I don't want to

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to Rav Pappa:
According to you, who say
that paying a creditor is a מצוה,
if the debtor said: "I don't want to do a מצוה,"
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא לְרַב פָּפָּא: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ פְּרִיעַת בַּעַל חוֹב מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about רב פפא's view that repaying a debt is a מצוה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, and how, a debtor can be forced to pay if repaying is only a מצוה and he refuses to do it.

steps.title: רב פפא brings a ברייתא about forcing positive מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers from a ברייתא: the rule of lashes applies to לא תעשה, but for מצות עשה like סוכה and לולב, בית דין deals differently with someone who refuses.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned: When is this said? For negative מצוות. But for positive מצוות, for example when they tell him "Make a סוכה" and he doesn't, or "Take a לולב" and he doesn't...
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers by quoting a ברייתא about a person who refuses to do a מצות עשה. The quote continues in the next lines, where we learn what בית דין does to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא separates the punishment for breaking a לא תעשה from the case of someone refusing a מצות עשה. רב פפא is showing that refusing a מצות עשה is not left alone: בית דין can force a person to do it, so the debtor can be forced to pay too.

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying מצות עשה don't matter. It is saying they are handled in a different way than the lashes given for a לא תעשה.
